newsitem.title: SUDAN: Sudan to try opposition leaders for attacks.
newsitem.headline: Sudan to try opposition leaders for attacks.

text.p: Sudan on Wednesday said it would put on trial nine opposition leaders in absentia, including former prime minister Sadeq al-Mahdi, on charges of waging war against the state with the help of hostile countries.

The charges are in connection with attacks last month by a rebel alliance on Sudan's eastern borders. Sudan has accused Ethiopia, Eritrea and Uganda of helping the rebels but the three countries deny the charge.

Sudanese Prosecutor General Abdel-Rahman Ibrahim al-Khalifa was quoted by the official news agency SUNA as saying the opposition leaders would also face charges of taking part in criminal and terrorist activity. He said 454 lawsuits had been raised against the nine men.
The men are members of the National Democratic Alliance (NDA), an umbrella group that brings together northern and southern opponents of Khartoum's Islamist government.

Among the men who face the charges are the leader of the Sudan People's Liberation Army John Garang, head of the Democratic Unionist Party Mohammed Osman al-Mirghani, three former ministers, and three former senior army officers.
Khalifa heads the government-appointed committee in charge of investigating alleged crimes committed during the attacks.
Sudan says many atrocities were committed against Sudanese citizens by the attackers who it maintains were mainly Ethiopian troops.
An official report carried by SUNA on Wednesday accused Ethiopia of looting, rape and killings in two towns Sudan says were seized last month by Ethiopian and Khartoum opposition forces.
Ethiopia has denied charges by the Khartoum government that it was behind the rebel attacks, which gained momentum last month with the fall of Kirmuk and Qissan along its border with Sudan.
